title: B24116640167
paper_title: WLAN 组网中网络吞吐量建模

strengths: RF pipeline keeps StandardScaler/OneHotEncoder inside fitted pipeline after outer train/test split
reports RF and LSTM MSE for both 2AP and 3AP
risks: LSTM preprocessing is fit on the whole data before train_test_split
LSTM reshapes tabular rows to one timestep, so it cannot learn actual temporal dependencies despite the LSTM name
rows from multiple WLAN experiments are not group-held-out

route: RF / SGD linear regression / LSTM predict PHY Rate
floor-map predicted PHY Rate back to (MCS,NSS)
strengths: recognizes high SINR should permit higher MCS and more streams
risks: multi-interferer SINR code subtracts several negative dBm vectors directly instead of summing linear interference power
mixed-mode SINR is formed by adding two SINR quantities without time weighting/physical derivation
PHY Rate to (MCS,NSS) inverse is non-injective; floor lookup resolves equal-rate ties by dictionary/order, not evidence
StandardScaler for SGD is fit before split
LSTM uses one-timestep pseudo-sequences and full-data preprocessing

route: formula baseline from PHY Rate, PER, seq_time/test_dur
strengths: states a useful physical baseline throughput ≈ PHYRate*(1-PER)*airtime fraction
compares several regressors and kernel choices
risks: training uses true seq_time/PHY-related intermediates while test construction uses Q1/Q2 predictions, creating oracle-intermediate deployment shift unless OOF predictions train the final model
SVR preprocessor is fit before train_test_split
LSTM again has one timestep and preprocessing leakage
reported 3AP polynomial-SVR MSE=12.48 with MAE=7.30 violates MSE >= MAE^2
paper says RBF is best among kernels and later LSTM is best overall, but its own polynomial-SVR 3AP MSE=12.48 would contradict those selections if the number were correct
several Q3 figure captions incorrectly say PHY_Rate although section claims throughput

verified_text_evidence.claim: Q1 selects 10-layer/5-layer LSTM by validation MSE
visible LSTM code fits preprocessing before split and reshapes each row to one timestep
Q2 formulas mix ratio-domain and dB-style SINR descriptions across synchronous/asynchronous/mixed modes
visible multi-AP SINR code returns rssi_0-rssi_1-rssi_2 directly
SGD StandardScaler fit_transform occurs before split
PHY-rate inverse lookup selects the last lower/equal tuple from a table containing duplicate rates
Q3 explicitly uses predicted seq_time and mapped PHY Rate in formula-based test throughput construction
SVR ColumnTransformer fit_transform occurs before split
3AP polynomial SVM table reports MSE 12.48 and MAE 7.30
narrative selects RBF among SVMs and LSTM overall despite conflicting polynomial-SVM table value

transfer_lessons: An LSTM/RNN needs a real ordered sequence axis. Shape (n,1,p) is a one-step nonlinear network, not evidence of learned temporal memory.
For multiple interferers, convert every dBm power to linear mW/W and sum there before computing SINR.
Never invert a non-injective PHY-rate table to a unique (MCS,NSS) tuple without additional constraints/evidence.
For Q1/Q2→Q3 cascades, train downstream models on OOF upstream predictions and report full-chain holdout performance.
Automatically apply metric identities such as MSE >= MAE^2 and RMSE=sqrt(MSE) to catch impossible tables before paper export.
If a simple physics formula exists, keep it as an explicit baseline and justify any ML layer by residual improvement on untouched groups.
